icount_spin.elf: icount_spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c icount_spin.S -o icount_spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) icount_spin.o -o $@

handoff.elf: handoff.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff.S -o handoff.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff.o -o $@

handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andes-sim.specs $< -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andes-sim.specs $< -o $@

# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andes-sim.specs $< -o $@

# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
               $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andes-sim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andes-sim.specs \
               $(RUNTIME_DIR)/roi.h
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

# Markerless GEMM twin (gemm_modes.md F2). Explicit rule, NOT in
# RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the pattern rule would look for a nonexistent
# rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same source, same link as the marked V fixtures,
# plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS (drops the ROI marker HINTs).
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andes-sim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@

dump: spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff_exit.elf

clean:
	rm -f spin.o spin.elf handoff.o handoff.elf handoff_exit.o handoff_exit.elf \
	      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
	      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

content.text:
Done. Here is the program and the proof.

## The program: `tests/fixtures/break_mscratch.S`

Bare-metal, single privilege (M), no async interrupt, no trap, no paging, no atomics. It only uses `mscratch` (CSR 0x340) - the standard M-mode software scratch register - across the ROI:

```asm
li   a1, 0xCAFEBABEDEADBEEF
csrw mscratch, a1        # stash a value BEFORE the ROI (QEMU leg)
slti x0, x0, 0x5A0       # ENTER ROI -> hand off to vsim
csrr a0, mscratch        # read it back INSIDE the ROI
csrw mscratch, 0xBADC... # overwrite it INSIDE the ROI
slti x0, x0, 0x5A1       # EXIT -> vsim drains + exits
```

## Proof (the simulator's own `--verify` oracle flags it)

```
[state-diff] x10: ref=0xcafebabedeadbeef got=0x0
[state-diff] FAIL: 1 mismatch(es) (110 fields compared)
```

`a0` (x10) read `mscratch` inside the ROI: pure-QEMU = the stashed value, vsim = `0x0`. The value never crossed the handoff.

## Root cause (two halves, same CSR)

1. **Resume gap** - `resume_driver.hpp:115` restores `mstatus/mtvec/mcycle/minstret/fcsr` (+`dcsr.prv`/PMP for S/U) but never writes `mscratch`. So the in-ROI read returns vsim's reset value.
2. **Drain gap** - `state_drain.hpp:75` (`drain_with_passthrough`) re-reads GPRs/FPR/V-CSRs/mcycle/minstret from vsim but passes `mscratch` through from the QEMU1 snapshot. So the in-ROI write is silently dropped from the drained state.

## Why this is not just "a known limitation"

The notebook's core rule (cell-5) says a vsim ROI is safe if it is single-privilege, trap-free, paging-off, PMP-static, no-semihosting, no-atomics, no-MMIO. **My program satisfies every one of those** and is still silently wrong. The envelope list is incomplete - it omits "do not use a drained-but-unrestored M-CSR (`mscratch`, `mepc`, ... ) across the ROI." `mscratch` is listed in the inventory (cell-6/cell-17) as "carried but not restored," but it has no L-id and is framed as a *trap* concern; a plain trap-free program using the M-mode scratch register is exactly the case the docs say is supported.

Three genuinely new findings fall out:
- **Drain gap** (write-side loss) is undocumented (L4 only covers the trap triple).
- **`--verify` is blind to it**: `state_diff.cpp:22` excludes passthrough CSRs ("counters and passthrough CSRs excluded"), so a program that leaves its result in `mscratch` produces a wrong drained state that `--verify` rates PASS.
- **The guard fixture is dead**: `rt_csr_survival.S` was written to check exactly this ("mscratch/mtvec/mepc survive QEMU1 -> vsim -> QEMU2"), but its `phase_c` readback sits *after* the exit marker. With the QEMU2 leg deleted, vsim drains+exits at the exit marker, so `phase_c` never runs. This property has been unguarded since the 3-phase design was removed.

This is L23-worthy for the notebook (per your limitations-routing convention) if you want me to write it up.

## On the toolchain

1	// Oracle differential compare (verify_oracle F2): field-wise diff of two
2	// drained hybrid_state_v1 records -- the QEMU oracle's exit-boundary drain
3	// (ref) against the hybrid run's vsim drain (got).
4	//
5	// Compare policy, fixed by what vsim's drain freshly reads (state_drain.hpp
6	// drain_with_passthrough):
7	//   strict:  magic/version/flags/hart_id/priv (identity), pc, gpr[0..31];
8	//            fpr[0..31] under FLAG_FP; vstart/vtype/vl/vlenb/vxsat/vxrm/vcsr
9	//            and the vreg bytes under FLAG_V.
10	//   skipped: mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch, medeleg,
11	//            mideleg, mip, mie, satp, pmpcfg[], pmpaddr[] -- passthrough on
12	//            the vsim side (copied from QEMU1's ENTRY snapshot, never
13	//            re-read), so comparing them would test entry-vs-exit.
14	//   masked:  mcycle, minstret, mcycle/minstret_at_measure_start -- the
15	//            engines count cycles/insns differently by design.
16	#ifndef ANDES_SIM_STATE_DIFF_HPP
17	#define ANDES_SIM_STATE_DIFF_HPP
18	
19	#include <string>
20	#include <vector>
21	
22	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
23	
24	namespace andes_sim {
25	
26	// One strictly-compared field that differs: "pc", "x5", "f31", "vl",
27	// "v3[7]" (register + byte offset), "flags", ...
28	struct FieldDiff {
29	  std::string field;
30	  unsigned long long ref = 0;
31	  unsigned long long got = 0;
32	};
33	
34	struct DiffReport {
35	  int compared = 0;  // count of strictly compared fields
36	  std::vector<FieldDiff> diffs;
37	  bool ok() const { return diffs.empty(); }
38	};
39	
40	// compare_trap_cause (cosim_redesign F6, lock-step): also compare mepc and
41	// mcause -- the well-defined trap fields that reveal a mishandled trap. Still
42	// EXCLUDES mtval (implementation-defined for illegal insns) and mstatus
43	// (dirty-bit differences), which would false-positive across QEMU vs RTL.
44	// Default false preserves the hybrid-ROI policy above (trap CSRs passthrough).
45	DiffReport diff_states(const hybrid_state_v1& ref, const hybrid_state_v1& got,
46	                       bool compare_trap_cause = false);
47	
48	// Print `r` as "[state-diff] ..." lines: one per mismatch, then the
49	// PASS/FAIL verdict. Shared by the state-diff subcommand and run --verify.
50	void print_diff_report(const DiffReport& r);
51	
52	}  // namespace andes_sim
53	
54	#endif  // ANDES_SIM_STATE_DIFF_HPP

---
name: reference-hybrid-unit-test-host-build
description: Fast host g++ build+run command for hybrid doctest unit tests (no container)
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 170e2aea-625a-4764-89fa-e0722f44012b
---

The `verilator/tests/hybrid/*.test.cpp` doctest unit tests are header-only
(C++20 + ABI header) and run directly on the host - no podman/Verilator needed.
Build+run one with:

```sh
cd /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim
g++ -std=c++20 -I verilator/src -I verilator/tests/hybrid -I include \
    -I verilator/external/doctest/doctest \
    verilator/tests/hybrid/resume_driver.test.cpp -o /tmp/t && /tmp/t
```

`-I verilator/tests/hybrid` is only needed for tests that include the shared
`recording_bus.hpp` (e.g. state_drain). This is the fast RED/GREEN loop; the
canonical container/ctest path is only required for the e2e suite.

Exceptions that do NOT link on the host: `qemu_handback.test.cpp` (needs libfmt:
`undefined reference to fmt::v11::...`), and the SystemC-dependent ones
(`*_smoke.cpp`, `shared_mem_offset.test.cpp`). Skip those on host.

vsim rebuild after editing `src/hybrid/*.hpp` or `src/simulator.hpp`:
`bash scripts/build_vsim.sh` (podman; incremental, recompiles `main.cpp.o` only,
RTL is cached - ~30s). Then e2e: `JOBS=8 FILTER=rt_c_v bash scripts/run_e2e.sh`.

aiTitle: Write program to test andes-sim robustness

content.content:
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# End-to-end harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim (2-phase, no QEMU2 handback).
3	#
4	# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
5	# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
6	# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
7	# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
8	# fine with it.
9	#
10	# Env:
11	#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
12	#   TRIGGER_MODE    marker | pc (default marker).
13	#   ROI_START       pc mode switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol in
14	#                   $VSIM_ELF. If BOTH ROI_START and ROI_END are unset, they
15	#                   are auto-derived from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via
16	#                   objdump (see roi_markers_from_disasm) -- the bulk runner
17	#                   relies on this; ./andes-sim run always passes them explicitly.
18	#   ROI_END         pc mode switch-out PC, same forms / same auto-derivation.
19	#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
20	#   VERIFY=1        opt-in differential verification (default off): re-run
21	#                   the ELF on pure QEMU with the plugin draining at the ROI
22	#                   exit boundary (the oracle), then `andes-sim state-diff`
23	#                   the oracle state against the vsim drain. Any divergence
24	#                   in what vsim freshly drains (pc/GPRs/FPRs/V) fails the
25	#                   test; counters and passthrough CSRs are excluded.
26	#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
27	#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
28	#   CHECK_PRIV=<0|1|3>         assert both drained state files carry this
29	#                              privilege (L6: 0=U, 1=S, 3=M).
30	#   WARMUP_ICOUNT              gem5-style warmup window. When set and > 0,
31	#                              passes --vsim-warmup-icount K to vsim and
32	#                              prints a [warmup] line carrying the captured
33	#                              (mcycle_at_measure_start, minstret_at_measure_start)
34	#                              pair from the drained state file.
35	#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.
36	#   QEMU_CPU        -cpu argument for both QEMU legs (default
37	#                   andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512, pairing the default vsim
38	#                   engine). Override together with VSIM_BIN to run a
39	#                   fixture on another engine, e.g. the S/U-capable
40	#                   ax66_makatau for the rt_priv_* fixtures (the default
41	#                   ax45mpv_premium RTL is M-mode-only).
42	
43	set -euo pipefail
44	
45	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
46	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"
47	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/roi.sh"
48	
49	FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
50	TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
51	TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-marker}"
52	QEMU_CPU="${QEMU_CPU:-andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512}"
53	
54	hybrid_resolve_paths
55	
56	NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
57	NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"
58	
59	case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
60	  marker) ;;
61	  pc)
62	    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
63	      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
64	      exit 77
65	    fi
66	    # ROI_START / ROI_END name the two switch PCs (0x address or symbol in
67	    # $VSIM_ELF). ./andes-sim run always passes them explicitly. When a caller
68	    # leaves BOTH unset (e.g. the bulk runner scripts/run_e2e.sh), derive them
69	    # from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via objdump, so pc mode needs no
70	    # per-fixture config and no planted boundary symbols. A partial set or a
71	    # derivation miss falls through to roi_resolve_pair's required-vars error.
72	    if [ -z "${ROI_START:-}" ] && [ -z "${ROI_END:-}" ]; then
73	      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
74	      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
75	      if command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
76	         && MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")"); then
77	        ROI_START="0x${MARKERS%% *}"
78	        ROI_END="0x${MARKERS##* }"
79	        export ROI_START ROI_END
80	      fi
81	    fi
82	    NM_OUT=$("$NM" --defined-only "$VSIM_ELF")
83	    roi_resolve_pair "$NM_OUT" "$FIXTURE pc" || exit 1
84	    ;;
85	  *)
86	    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (use marker|pc)"
87	    exit 1
88	    ;;
89	esac
90	
91	# 128 MB matches the QEMU virt machine default; vsim uses the same size.
92	SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
93	SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
94	STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
95	STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
96	STATE_ORACLE=$(mktemp)
97	SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
98	trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$STATE_ORACLE" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
99	truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"
100	
101	PLUGIN_ARGS="outfile=$STATE_QEMU"
102	VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=()
103	if [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ]; then
104	  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC"
105	  VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=(--hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC")
106	fi
107	
108	# F21: forward --vsim-warmup-icount when caller asked for a warmup window.
109	VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS=()
110	if [ "${WARMUP_ICOUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
111	  VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS=(--vsim-warmup-icount "$WARMUP_ICOUNT")
112	fi
113	
114	# Optional ROI kanata logging: hsim sets KANATA_FILE (and optionally
115	# OBJDUMP_FILE) when the user passes --kanata. vsim's --kanata-roi auto-
116	# derives the window from the resume PC and the unique exit PC.
117	VSIM_KANATA_ARGS=()
118	if [ -n "${KANATA_FILE:-}" ]; then
119	  VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--kanata "$KANATA_FILE" --kanata-roi)
120	  if [ -n "${OBJDUMP_FILE:-}" ]; then
121	    VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--objdump "$OBJDUMP_FILE")
122	  fi
123	fi
124	
125	echo "[$FIXTURE 1/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 1: drain entry state"
126	set +e
127	"$VSIM_QEMU" \
128	  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
129	  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
130	  -cpu "$QEMU_CPU" \
131	  -nographic \
132	  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# End-to-end harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim (2-phase, no QEMU2 handback).
#
# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
# fine with it.
#
# Env:
#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
#   TRIGGER_MODE    marker | pc (default marker).
#   ROI_START       pc mode switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol in
#                   $VSIM_ELF. If BOTH ROI_START and ROI_END are unset, they
#                   are auto-derived from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via
#                   objdump (see roi_markers_from_disasm) -- the bulk runner
#                   relies on this; ./andes-sim run always passes them explicitly.
#   ROI_END         pc mode switch-out PC, same forms / same auto-derivation.
#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
#   VERIFY=1        opt-in differential verification (default off): re-run
#                   the ELF on pure QEMU with the plugin draining at the ROI
#                   exit boundary (the oracle), then `andes-sim state-diff`
#                   the oracle state against the vsim drain. Any divergence
#                   in what vsim freshly drains (pc/GPRs/FPRs/V) fails the
#                   test; counters and passthrough CSRs are excluded.
#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
#   CHECK_PRIV=<0|1|3>         assert both drained state files carry this
#                              privilege (L6: 0=U, 1=S, 3=M).
#   WARMUP_ICOUNT              gem5-style warmup window. When set and > 0,
#                              passes --vsim-warmup-icount K to vsim and
#                              prints a [warmup] line carrying the captured
#                              (mcycle_at_measure_start, minstret_at_measure_start)
#                              pair from the drained state file.
#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.
#   QEMU_CPU        -cpu argument for both QEMU legs (default
#                   andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512, pairing the default vsim
#                   engine). Override together with VSIM_BIN to run a
#                   fixture on another engine, e.g. the S/U-capable
#                   ax66_makatau for the rt_priv_* fixtures (the default
#                   ax45mpv_premium RTL is M-mode-only).

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/roi.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-marker}"
QEMU_CPU="${QEMU_CPU:-andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512}"

hybrid_resolve_paths

NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"

case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
  marker) ;;
  pc)
    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
      exit 77
    fi
    # ROI_START / ROI_END name the two switch PCs (0x address or symbol in
    # $VSIM_ELF). ./andes-sim run always passes them explicitly. When a caller
    # leaves BOTH unset (e.g. the bulk runner scripts/run_e2e.sh), derive them
    # from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via objdump, so pc mode needs no
    # per-fixture config and no planted boundary symbols. A partial set or a
    # derivation miss falls through to roi_resolve_pair's required-vars error.
    if [ -z "${ROI_START:-}" ] && [ -z "${ROI_END:-}" ]; then
      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
      if command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
         && MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")"); then
        ROI_START="0x${MARKERS%% *}"
        ROI_END="0x${MARKERS##* }"
        export ROI_START ROI_END
      fi
    fi
    NM_OUT=$("$NM" --defined-only "$VSIM_ELF")
    roi_resolve_pair "$NM_OUT" "$FIXTURE pc" || exit 1
    ;;
  *)
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (use marker|pc)"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

# 128 MB matches the QEMU virt machine default; vsim uses the same size.
SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
STATE_ORACLE=$(mktemp)
SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$STATE_ORACLE" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

PLUGIN_ARGS="outfile=$STATE_QEMU"
VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=()
if [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ]; then
  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC"
  VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=(--hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC")
fi

# F21: forward --vsim-warmup-icount when caller asked for a warmup window.
VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS=()
if [ "${WARMUP_ICOUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
  VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS=(--vsim-warmup-icount "$WARMUP_ICOUNT")
fi

# Optional ROI kanata logging: hsim sets KANATA_FILE (and optionally
# OBJDUMP_FILE) when the user passes --kanata. vsim's --kanata-roi auto-
# derives the window from the resume PC and the unique exit PC.
VSIM_KANATA_ARGS=()
if [ -n "${KANATA_FILE:-}" ]; then
  VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--kanata "$KANATA_FILE" --kanata-roi)
  if [ -n "${OBJDUMP_FILE:-}" ]; then
    VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--objdump "$OBJDUMP_FILE")
  fi
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 1/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 1: drain entry state"
set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu "$QEMU_CPU" \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,$PLUGIN_ARGS" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
QEMU1_RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$QEMU1_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
  exit 1
fi

if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 did not produce state"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 2/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] vsim: resume + drain"
set +e
timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
  "${VSIM_TRIG_ARGS[@]}" \
  "${VSIM_KANATA_ARGS[@]}" \
  "${VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS[@]}" </dev/null >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1
VSIM_RC=$?
set -e

# vsim drained on the exit trigger and exited 200 (kExitHandoffToQemu).
# Anything else is a hard failure: the cycle figure is only valid when vsim
# drained cleanly.
if [ "$VSIM_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim expected exit 200 (drain), got $VSIM_RC"
  echo "--- sim log ---"
  cat "$SIM_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

# Kernel cycles (always) + opt-in monotonic check. Offsets locked by
# state_abi_check.h (mcycle@624, minstret@632). vsim restores mcycle from
# QEMU 1's drain then counts real clock cycles, so vsim_mcycle - qemu1_mcycle
# is the measured region's cycle count. Runs before the RC gate so the
# verdict is independent of any downstream-phase failure.
read_u64_le() { od -A n -j "$1" -N 8 -t u8 "$2" | tr -d ' \n'; }
if [ -s "$STATE_VSIM" ] && [ -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  Q1_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le 624 "$STATE_QEMU")
  Q1_MINST=$(read_u64_le  632 "$STATE_QEMU")
  V_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le  624 "$STATE_VSIM")
  V_MINST=$(read_u64_le   632 "$STATE_VSIM")
  echo "[$FIXTURE kernel_cycles] $((V_MCYCLE - Q1_MCYCLE))  (vsim mcycle=$V_MCYCLE - qemu1 mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE)"
  # F21: when WARMUP_ICOUNT is set, surface the snapshot pair so callers
  # can verify the warmup window without re-parsing the state file.
  # Offsets locked by include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h (F13, ceiling 128):
  #   mcycle_at_measure_start@5440, minstret_at_measure_start@5448.
  if [ "${WARMUP_ICOUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
    MS_MC=$(read_u64_le 5440 "$STATE_VSIM")
    MS_MI=$(read_u64_le 5448 "$STATE_VSIM")
    echo "[$FIXTURE warmup] K=$WARMUP_ICOUNT mcycle_at_measure_start=$MS_MC minstret_at_measure_start=$MS_MI"
  fi
  # L6: privilege survives the handoff. priv@24 locked by state_abi_check.h.
  if [ -n "${CHECK_PRIV:-}" ]; then
    Q1_PRIV=$(read_u64_le 24 "$STATE_QEMU")
    V_PRIV=$(read_u64_le  24 "$STATE_VSIM")
    echo "[$FIXTURE priv] qemu1=$Q1_PRIV vsim=$V_PRIV expected=$CHECK_PRIV"
    if [ "$Q1_PRIV" != "$CHECK_PRIV" ] || [ "$V_PRIV" != "$CHECK_PRIV" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: drained priv mismatch (expected $CHECK_PRIV)"
      exit 1
    fi
  fi
  if [ "${CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] qemu1: mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE minstret=$Q1_MINST"
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] vsim:  mcycle=$V_MCYCLE minstret=$V_MINST"
    if [ "$V_MCYCLE" -le "$Q1_MCYCLE" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: mcycle not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    if [ "$V_MINST" -le "$Q1_MINST" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: minstret not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] PASS: strictly increasing"
  fi
fi

# verify_oracle F3 (opt-in, default off): differential check against a
# pure-QEMU oracle. The same ELF re-runs on QEMU alone -- clean memory, so
# NO shared mmap (reusing it would leak the hybrid run's post-ROI bytes
# into the oracle's boot) -- with the plugin draining at the ROI exit
# boundary. state-diff then compares everything vsim freshly drains.
if [ "${VERIFY:-0}" = "1" ]; then
  ANDES_SIM_BIN="${ANDES_SIM_BIN:-$TOP_ROOT/build/andes-sim}"
  if [ ! -x "$ANDES_SIM_BIN" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: VERIFY=1 needs $ANDES_SIM_BIN (run scripts/build_driver.sh)"
    exit 1
  fi
  ORACLE_TRIG="exit_marker=1"
  [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ] && ORACLE_TRIG="exit_pc=0x$EXIT_PC"
  # Sample at vsim's ACTUAL halt point: the DMI halt lands a variable 0-3
  # insns past the trigger, so the oracle must drain at the pc vsim's state
  # file reports (offset 16, locked by state_abi_check.h), not at trigger+1.
  VSIM_PC=$(printf '0x%x' "$(read_u64_le 16 "$STATE_VSIM")")
  ORACLE_TRIG="$ORACLE_TRIG,drain_pc=$VSIM_PC"

  echo "[$FIXTURE verify mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] oracle: pure QEMU drains at ROI exit (pc=$VSIM_PC)"
  set +e
  "$VSIM_QEMU" \
    -machine andes_ae350 \
    -cpu "$QEMU_CPU" \
    -nographic \
    -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
    -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
    -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_ORACLE,$ORACLE_TRIG" \
    </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
  ORACLE_RC=$?
  set -e
  if [ "$ORACLE_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: oracle QEMU expected exit 200 on drain, got $ORACLE_RC"
    exit 1
  fi

  set +e
  DIFF_OUT=$("$ANDES_SIM_BIN" state-diff "$STATE_ORACLE" "$STATE_VSIM" 2>&1)
  DIFF_RC=$?
  set -e
  printf '%s\n' "$DIFF_OUT"
  if [ "$DIFF_RC" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim drain diverges from the QEMU oracle"
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "[$FIXTURE verify] PASS: vsim drain matches the QEMU oracle"
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE PASS] 2-phase handoff complete (QEMU 1 drain -> vsim drain)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build vsim inside the env-stage container image.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
VSIM_DIR="$ROOT/verilator"

if [[ ! -f "$VSIM_DIR/Dockerfile" ]]; then
  echo "missing $VSIM_DIR/Dockerfile - run 'git submodule update --init --recursive'" >&2
  exit 1
fi

cd "$VSIM_DIR"

podman build --target env -t vsim-env:latest .
podman run --rm \
  -v "$PWD:/work" \
  -v "$ROOT/include:/include:ro" \
  -w /work localhost/vsim-env:latest ./build.sh

+// across the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. A value stashed before the ROI is readable
+// inside it (ResumeDriver restores mscratch) and a value written inside the ROI
+// is captured at drain (StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough re-reads it).
-// Phase A (QEMU1): write distinguishable values to mscratch, mtvec, and
-//                  mepc, then trigger the entry handoff.
-// Phase B (vsim):  no-op.  vsim does not modify these CSRs; they must
-//                  pass through the input-state snapshot kept by
-//                  HandoffController and arrive at QEMU 2 unchanged.
-// Phase C (QEMU2): csrr each CSR back into a GPR, compare. Exit code is
-//                  the CSR index of the first mismatch (1=mscratch,
+// History: this fixture predates the 2-phase redesign. It used to read the CSRs
+// back in a `phase_c` AFTER the exit marker and exit with the index of the
+// first mismatch -- but once the QEMU2 handback leg was removed, vsim drains and
+// exits AT the exit marker, so phase_c never ran and the guard was silently
+// dead. The check now lives INSIDE the ROI, where the vsim leg actually runs.
-// mtvec is written with a 4-byte aligned value (mode=Direct) so QEMU
-// accepts it without rounding the low bits.
+// Self-check (works in the plain e2e harness, no --verify needed): read
+// mscratch back inside the ROI and compare against the stashed sentinel (held
+// in a1, which the GPR restore round-trips). On a regressed restore the values
+// differ, so the fixture spins -- vsim never reaches the exit marker, times
+// out, and the harness reports "vsim expected exit 200". With VERIFY=1 the
+// oracle additionally compares a0 (the read-back) and the mscratch CSR field
+// (the in-ROI write) against a pure-QEMU run.
+// Only mscratch is asserted: mtvec is restored but not re-drained, and
+// deferred to the L3/L4 envelope work -- see docs/andes_sim_limitations.ipynb).
+    csrw    mscratch, a1            // stash sentinel BEFORE the ROI (QEMU leg)
+    slti    x0, x0, 0x5A0           // ENTER ROI -> hand off to vsim

The vsim phase is assumed trap-free and PMP-static; if a future workload needs traps or dynamic PMP inside the ROI, `ResumeDriver` must be extended.

**Privilege (L6)**: the handoff carries the real privilege level. The plugin drains the gdbstub `priv` register, `ResumeDriver` read-modify-writes `dcsr.prv` before `dret` (and verifies the write took -- an M-mode-only RTL like the default `ax45mpv_premium`, `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`, WARL-pins the field, and the resume aborts with a pick-an-S/U-capable-engine error), and `StateDrain` reads `dcsr.prv` back at the exit halt. For S/U handoffs the producer's PMP block (64 `pmpaddr` + the 8 even `pmpcfg`) is also mirrored into the hart, because with PMP implemented and no matching entry every S/U access faults; M-mode handoffs keep PMP pass-through-only (L2). The `rt_priv_smode`/`rt_priv_umode` fixtures run on the S/U-capable `ax66_makatau` engine paired with QEMU `-cpu andes-ax66` (see `scripts/run_e2e.sh`); the ROI itself must still be trap-free, single-privilege, and paging-off (S-mode CSRs are not transported).

## The core rule: the vsim measurement window (ROI) is very narrow

This is the single most important limitation. Everything in Tier 1 is a
consequence of it.

When execution hands off to vsim, the resume step writes back only a small
part of the CPU state. Read `resume_driver.hpp`: it restores GPRs,
FPRs, the V registers, PC, six CSRs - `mstatus`, `mtvec`,
`mcycle`, `minstret`, `fcsr` (since L20, 2026-06-12), and `mscratch`
(since L23, 2026-06-15) - plus, since
L6 (2026-06-13), the privilege level via `dcsr.prv` (write-verified) and,
for S/U-privilege handoffs only, the PMP block.
It does NOT write `satp`, `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`,
`medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie` - and for M-mode
handoffs PMP stays unrestored too (L2).

The cell below prints the complete CSR list the resume driver knows. Note
what is still missing: no `satp`, no `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`.

    "The QEMU1 plugin drains them into the struct, but `ResumeDriver`\n",

## State coverage: what the wire format carries

Inventory view of the ROI rule above. Everything below is checked against
`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (struct), the QEMU plugin drain
(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`), the vsim resume (`resume_driver.hpp`),
and the vsim drain (`state_drain.hpp`).

### Carried in `hybrid_state_v1`

- 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs
- `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags; added 2026-06-12, closing L20)
- 13 M-mode CSRs: `mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch,
  medeleg, mideleg, mip, mie, mcycle, minstret, satp`
- PMP: 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
- V extension: `vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, vreg[32], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr`
- F13 warmup metadata: `mcycle_at_measure_start`, `minstret_at_measure_start`
- `reserved[208]` = room for ~26 more `uint64` (wire format is version 2
  since L11 widened `vreg[]` to 128 bytes per register)

### NOT in the wire format at all

- All S-mode CSRs: `stvec, sepc, scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip,
  scounteren, senvcfg, stimecmp`
- HPM block: `mhpmcounter3..31`, `mhpmevent3..31`, `mcounteren,
  menvcfg, mcountinhibit, mconfigptr, misa, time`
- Every Andes-custom CSR (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec`, ...). See L21.

### Carried but NOT restored into vsim

The QEMU1 plugin drains them into the struct, but `ResumeDriver`
writes none of them into the vsim hart. They are dead during the ROI:

- `satp` (L3), `mepc / mcause / mtval` (L4), and `medeleg, mideleg,
  mip, mie` (L2/L4 -- trap/interrupt machinery). (`mscratch` left this
  set in L23: it is a side-effect-free software CSR and round-trips
  now.) PMP is restored only for S/U-privilege handoffs (L6,
  2026-06-13) -- without it an S/U ROI cannot fetch on a
  PMP-implementing core; M-mode handoffs keep PMP pass-through-only.

CSRs actually restored into vsim: `mstatus, mtvec, mscratch (L23),
mcycle, minstret, fcsr`, plus `dcsr.prv` (the privilege level, verified
after write) and the PMP block for S/U handoffs (`resume_driver.hpp`).
`mscratch` is also re-read at drain and compared by `--verify` (L23).

### Transport ceiling - why "all CSRs" is not free

Three surfaces, three ceilings:

| Surface         | Mechanism                                     | Ceiling |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
| QEMU1 drain     | plugin reads by NAME from gdbstub XML         | only CSRs the QEMU fork advertises |
| vsim resume     | DMI Abstract Cmd + Program Buffer (by number) | RO / WARL / locked bits will not take arbitrary values |
| vsim drain      | DMI Abstract read (by number)                 | general for any readable CSR |

Two structural blockers to "all CSRs":

1. Wire format is a fixed C struct; `reserved[208]` fits about 26 more
   `uint64`. Reaching the full M + S + HPM + Andes set needs a v2 layout.
2. Semantics, not just bits. Restore order and side effects already bite
   (`mstatus.FS/VS` gating, `vsetvl` atomicity for `vtype/vl`). Writing
   `satp` flushes the TLB; Andes `mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` toggle caches,
   prefetchers, branch prediction and may be RO or locked when written
   via the debug module mid-run. Those are exactly the CSRs that shape
   the cycle figure.

Verdict: extending the wire format to a bounded set in this way is
feasible - the L20 fix is the worked example (one `uint64` carved from
`reserved[]`, drained by name, restored via the existing
abstract-or-PB write, read back at drain). S-mode trap CSRs and a
chosen Andes microarch subset can follow the same recipe.
"All RISC-V CSRs including Andes-specific" is not feasible without
redesigning the wire format and lifting the entire ROI envelope (L2-L6).

chosen Andes microarch subset can follow the same recipe.

### L23. mscratch (M-mode software scratch CSR) did not round-trip  (new 2026-06-15)

- When it bit: any bare-metal, trap-free, single-privilege ROI -- the
  envelope cell-5 calls *supported* -- that used `mscratch` (CSR 0x340)
  across the handoff. `mscratch` is the M-mode software scratch register, a
  side-effect-free read/write CSR; using it needs no trap, no interrupt,
  no paging. It was drained by QEMU1 but never restored into vsim and never
  re-read at drain, so:
  1. a value stashed before the ROI read back as the vsim reset value
     inside the ROI (the **resume gap**); and
  2. a value written inside the ROI was dropped from the drained state,
     which silently kept QEMU1's pre-ROI value (the **drain gap**).
  `--verify` could not catch (2): `state_diff` excluded `mscratch` as a
  "passthrough CSR". The repo's own guard (`rt_csr_survival.S`) had gone
  dead in the 2-phase redesign (its readback `phase_c` sat after the exit
  marker, on the deleted QEMU2 leg), so nothing flagged the regression.
- Why it mattered: this broke a workload sitting ENTIRELY inside the
  "safe" envelope, so that envelope list was incomplete.
- Status: RESOLVED (2026-06-15). `mscratch` round-trips end to end:
  - vsim resume: restored via the tolerant CSR write right after `mtvec`
    (`resume_driver.hpp`); no FP/V gate -- it is plain M-mode state.
  - vsim drain: re-read from the hart in `drain_with_passthrough`, so an
    in-ROI write is captured (`state_drain.hpp`).
  - `--verify`: `state_diff` strictly compares `mscratch` in the hybrid
    policy (still excluded in lock-step, where it is reset-vs-reset like
    `mstatus`/`mtval`).
  - guard: `tests/fixtures/rt_csr_survival.S` revived as a live 2-phase
    self-check; unit cases in `resume_driver.test.cpp`,
    `state_drain.test.cpp`, `state_diff_test.cpp`.
- Scope: only `mscratch`. The other drained-but-unrestored M-CSRs
  (`mepc/mcause/mtval/medeleg/mideleg/mip/mie`, `satp`) are trap / interrupt
  / paging machinery, deferred to the L3/L4 envelope work; `mtvec` is
  restored but still not re-drained.

- 13 M-mode CSRs: `mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch,
  medeleg, mideleg, mip, mie, mcycle, minstret, satp`
- PMP: 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
- V extension: `vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, vreg[32], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr`
- F13 warmup metadata: `mcycle_at_measure_start`, `minstret_at_measure_start`
- `reserved[208]` = room for ~26 more `uint64` (wire format is version 2
  since L11 widened `vreg[]` to 128 bytes per register)

### NOT in the wire format at all

- All S-mode CSRs: `stvec, sepc, scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip,
  scounteren, senvcfg, stimecmp`
- HPM block: `mhpmcounter3..31`, `mhpmevent3..31`, `mcounteren,
  menvcfg, mcountinhibit, mconfigptr, misa, time`
- Every Andes-custom CSR (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec`, ...). See L21.

### Carried but NOT restored into vsim

The QEMU1 plugin drains them into the struct, but `ResumeDriver`
writes none of them into the vsim hart. They are dead during the ROI:

- `satp` (L3), `mepc / mcause / mtval` (L4), and `medeleg, mideleg,
  mip, mie` (L2/L4 -- trap/interrupt machinery). (`mscratch` left this
  set in L23: it is a side-effect-free software CSR and round-trips
  now.) PMP is restored only for S/U-privilege handoffs (L6,
  2026-06-13) -- without it an S/U ROI cannot fetch on a
  PMP-implementing core; M-mode handoffs keep PMP pass-through-only.

CSRs actually restored into vsim: `mstatus, mtvec, mscratch (L23),
mcycle, minstret, fcsr`, plus `dcsr.prv` (the privilege level, verified
after write) and the PMP block for S/U handoffs (`resume_driver.hpp`).
`mscratch` is also re-read at drain and compared by `--verify` (L23).

### Transport ceiling - why "all CSRs" is not free

Three surfaces, three ceilings:

| Surface         | Mechanism                                     | Ceiling |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
| QEMU1 drain     | plugin reads by NAME from gdbstub XML         | only CSRs the QEMU fork advertises |
| vsim resume     | DMI Abstract Cmd + Program Buffer (by number) | RO / WARL / locked bits will not take arbitrary values |
| vsim drain      | DMI Abstract read (by number)                 | general for any readable CSR |

Two structural blockers to "all CSRs":

1. Wire format is a fixed C struct; `reserved[208]` fits about 26 more
   `uint64`. Reaching the full M + S + HPM + Andes set needs a v2 layout.
2. Semantics, not just bits. Restore order and side effects already bite
   (`mstatus.FS/VS` gating, `vsetvl` atomicity for `vtype/vl`). Writing
   `satp` flushes the TLB; Andes `mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` toggle caches,
   prefetchers, branch prediction and may be RO or locked when written
   via the debug module mid-run. Those are exactly the CSRs that shape
   the cycle figure.

Verdict: extending the wire format to a bounded set in this way is
feasible - the L20 fix is the worked example (one `uint64` carved from
`reserved[]`, drained by name, restored via the existing
abstract-or-PB write, read back at drain). S-mode trap CSRs and a
chosen Andes microarch subset can follow the same recipe.
"All RISC-V CSRs including Andes-specific" is not feasible without
redesigning the wire format and lifting the entire ROI envelope (L2-L6)."

   "source": "## State coverage: what the wire format carries

Inventory view of the ROI rule above. Everything below is checked against
`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (struct), the QEMU plugin drain
(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`), the vsim resume (`resume_driver.hpp`),
and the vsim drain (`state_drain.hpp`).

### Carried in `hybrid_state_v1`

- 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs
- `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags; added 2026-06-12, closing L20)
- 13 M-mode CSRs: `mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch,
  medeleg, mideleg, mip, mie, mcycle, minstret, satp`
- PMP: 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
- V extension: `vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, vreg[32], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr`
- F13 warmup metadata: `mcycle_at_measure_start`, `minstret_at_measure_start`
- `reserved[208]` = room for ~26 more `uint64` (wire format is version 2
  since L11 widened `vreg[]` to 128 bytes per register)

### NOT in the wire format at all

- All S-mode CSRs: `stvec, sepc, scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip,
  scounteren, senvcfg, stimecmp`
- HPM block: `mhpmcounter3..31`, `mhpmevent3..31`, `mcounteren,
  menvcfg, mcountinhibit, mconfigptr, misa, time`
- Every Andes-custom CSR (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec`, ...). See L21.

### Carried but NOT restored into vsim

The QEMU1 plugin drains them into the struct, but `ResumeDriver`
writes none of them into the vsim hart. They are dead during the ROI:

- `satp` (L3), `mepc / mcause / mtval` (L4), and `medeleg, mideleg,
  mip, mie` (L2/L4 -- trap/interrupt machinery). (`mscratch` left this
  set in L23: it is a side-effect-free software CSR and round-trips
  now.) PMP is restored only for S/U-privilege handoffs (L6,
  2026-06-13) -- without it an S/U ROI cannot fetch on a
  PMP-implementing core; M-mode handoffs keep PMP pass-through-only.

CSRs actually restored into vsim: `mstatus, mtvec, mscratch (L23),
mcycle, minstret, fcsr`, plus `dcsr.prv` (the privilege level, verified
after write) and the PMP block for S/U handoffs (`resume_driver.hpp`).
`mscratch` is also re-read at drain and compared by `--verify` (L23).

### Transport ceiling - why "all CSRs" is not free

Three surfaces, three ceilings:

| Surface         | Mechanism                                     | Ceiling |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
| QEMU1 drain     | plugin reads by NAME from gdbstub XML         | only CSRs the QEMU fork advertises |
| vsim resume     | DMI Abstract Cmd + Program Buffer (by number) | RO / WARL / locked bits will not take arbitrary values |
| vsim drain      | DMI Abstract read (by number)                 | general for any readable CSR |

Two structural blockers to "all CSRs":

1. Wire format is a fixed C struct; `reserved[208]` fits about 26 more
   `uint64`. Reaching the full M + S + HPM + Andes set needs a v2 layout.
2. Semantics, not just bits. Restore order and side effects already bite
   (`mstatus.FS/VS` gating, `vsetvl` atomicity for `vtype/vl`). Writing
   `satp` flushes the TLB; Andes `mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` toggle caches,
   prefetchers, branch prediction and may be RO or locked when written
   via the debug module mid-run. Those are exactly the CSRs that shape
   the cycle figure.

Verdict: extending the wire format to a bounded set in this way is
feasible - the L20 fix is the worked example (one `uint64` carved from
`reserved[]`, drained by name, restored via the existing
abstract-or-PB write, read back at drain). S-mode trap CSRs and a
chosen Andes microarch subset can follow the same recipe.
"All RISC-V CSRs including Andes-specific" is not feasible without
redesigning the wire format and lifting the entire ROI envelope (L2-L6)."

  supported - this is only about async interrupts.

  (QEMU is functional with no real cycles, the RTL is cycle-accurate), so
  each takes the same interrupt at a DIFFERENT retired-instruction index.

  record compares handler-vs-mainloop and the diff reports a flood of false
  divergences. Testbenches must be interrupt-free today.

   "source": "## State coverage: what the wire format carries

Inventory view of the ROI rule above. Everything below is checked against
`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (struct), the QEMU plugin drain
(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`), the vsim resume (`resume_driver.hpp`),
and the vsim drain (`state_drain.hpp`).

### Carried in `hybrid_state_v1`

- 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs
- `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags; added 2026-06-12, closing L20)
- 13 M-mode CSRs: `mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch,
  medeleg, mideleg, mip, mie, mcycle, minstret, satp`
- PMP: 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
- V extension: `vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, vreg[32], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr`
- F13 warmup metadata: `mcycle_at_measure_start`, `minstret_at_measure_start`
- `reserved[208]` = room for ~26 more `uint64` (wire format is version 2
  since L11 widened `vreg[]` to 128 bytes per register)

### NOT in the wire format at all

- All S-mode CSRs: `stvec, sepc, scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip,
  scounteren, senvcfg, stimecmp`
- HPM block: `mhpmcounter3..31`, `mhpmevent3..31`, `mcounteren,
  menvcfg, mcountinhibit, mconfigptr, misa, time`
- Every Andes-custom CSR (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec`, ...). See L21.

### Carried but NOT restored into vsim

The QEMU1 plugin drains them into the struct, but `ResumeDriver`
writes none of them into the vsim hart. They are dead during the ROI:

- `satp` (L3), `mepc / mcause / mtval` (L4), and `medeleg, mideleg,
  mip, mie` (L2/L4 -- trap/interrupt machinery). (`mscratch` left this
  set in L23: it is a side-effect-free software CSR and round-trips
  now.) PMP is restored only for S/U-privilege handoffs (L6,
  2026-06-13) -- without it an S/U ROI cannot fetch on a
  PMP-implementing core; M-mode handoffs keep PMP pass-through-only.

CSRs actually restored into vsim: `mstatus, mtvec, mscratch (L23),
mcycle, minstret, fcsr`, plus `dcsr.prv` (the privilege level, verified
after write) and the PMP block for S/U handoffs (`resume_driver.hpp`).
`mscratch` is also re-read at drain and compared by `--verify` (L23).

### Transport ceiling - why "all CSRs" is not free

Three surfaces, three ceilings:

| Surface         | Mechanism                                     | Ceiling |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
| QEMU1 drain     | plugin reads by NAME from gdbstub XML         | only CSRs the QEMU fork advertises |
| vsim resume     | DMI Abstract Cmd + Program Buffer (by number) | RO / WARL / locked bits will not take arbitrary values |
| vsim drain      | DMI Abstract read (by number)                 | general for any readable CSR |

Two structural blockers to "all CSRs":

1. Wire format is a fixed C struct; `reserved[208]` fits about 26 more
   `uint64`. Reaching the full M + S + HPM + Andes set needs a v2 layout.
2. Semantics, not just bits. Restore order and side effects already bite
   (`mstatus.FS/VS` gating, `vsetvl` atomicity for `vtype/vl`). Writing
   `satp` flushes the TLB; Andes `mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` toggle caches,
   prefetchers, branch prediction and may be RO or locked when written
   via the debug module mid-run. Those are exactly the CSRs that shape
   the cycle figure.

Verdict: extending the wire format to a bounded set in this way is
feasible - the L20 fix is the worked example (one `uint64` carved from
`reserved[]`, drained by name, restored via the existing
abstract-or-PB write, read back at drain). S-mode trap CSRs and a
chosen Andes microarch subset can follow the same recipe.
"All RISC-V CSRs including Andes-specific" is not feasible without
redesigning the wire format and lifting the entire ROI envelope (L2-L6)."

Honest scorecard for "is this a shippable commercial product today?".

gem5 + functional warmup) for a CPU vendor's hybrid sim offering.

**Overall: 4/10 as a shippable commercial product. ~7/10 as an internal
/ research tool inside its narrow design envelope.**

| Axis                                  | Score | Note |
|---------------------------------------|-------|------|
| Architecture clarity                  | 8/10  | Two-phase handoff is clean; shared ABI is a single header. |
| Engineering discipline                | 7/10  | TDD gate, doctest, parallel CI, a candid limitations doc. |
| State coverage (correctness surface)  | 3/10  | 22 documented limitations; only 6 CSRs round-trip into vsim. |

| Robustness / errors                   | 5/10  | `cmderr` is cleared and swallowed; only a private diagnostic side channel. |
| Docs / onboarding                     | 7/10  | `CLAUDE.md`, `USER_GUIDE.md`, and this notebook are unusually honest. |
| Test fixtures                         | 6/10  | Solid asm + C-runtime e2e; FP-rounding (rt_c_fcsr) and S/U-privilege (rt_priv_*) covered now; still no trap fixtures. |

   compares it. Still standing: `cmderr` is W1C-cleared so a partial CSR
   restore is observable only through a private counter

   transports since L6, 2026-06-13, on an S/U-capable engine), but "no
   traps, no paging, no semihosting inside the window" (L1-L5) still
   rules out every real OS-bearing benchmark - SPEC under Linux, any
   driver code, anything with page faults. The vplat runtime covers
   bare-metal I/O only.

   `mmsc_cfg / mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` transport (L21) is a
   credibility hit and an accuracy hazard - cache and prefetcher
   controls shape the cycle count.

   minstret, fcsr), plus `dcsr.prv` and - for S/U handoffs - the PMP

  is the release-blocker checklist; internally it is exemplary.
- SimPoint integration for whole-program cycle estimation (L14) is a
  real differentiator over a pure functional sim.

### Bottom line

release you need:

- traps + paging supported inside ROI (close L3, L4);
  ~~privilege transport (L6)~~ done 2026-06-13
- Andes vendor CSR transport (close L21)

- A proper error policy instead of `cmderr` swallowing
- The existing `--verify`/`--cosim` oracle (L15) extended to

(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`), the vsim resume (`resume_driver.hpp`),

- 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs
- `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags; added 2026-06-12, closing L20)
- 13 M-mode CSRs: `mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch,

Three surfaces, three ceilings:

| Surface         | Mechanism                                     | Ceiling |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
| QEMU1 drain     | plugin reads by NAME from gdbstub XML         | only CSRs the QEMU fork advertises |
| vsim resume     | DMI Abstract Cmd + Program Buffer (by number) | RO / WARL / locked bits will not take arbitrary values |
| vsim drain      | DMI Abstract read (by number)                 | general for any readable CSR |

Two structural blockers to "all CSRs":

1. Wire format is a fixed C struct; `reserved[208]` fits about 26 more

2. Semantics, not just bits. Restore order and side effects already bite

   the cycle figure.

abstract-or-PB write, read back at drain). S-mode trap CSRs and a
chosen Andes microarch subset can follow the same recipe.
"All RISC-V CSRs including Andes-specific" is not feasible without
redesigning the wire format and lifting the entire ROI envelope (L2-L6)."

  no paging. It was drained by QEMU1 but never restored into vsim and never
  re-read at drain, so:
  1. a value stashed before the ROI read back as the vsim reset value
     inside the ROI (the **resume gap**); and
  2. a value written inside the ROI was dropped from the drained state,
     which silently kept QEMU1's pre-ROI value (the **drain gap**).

  "passthrough CSR". The repo's own guard (`rt_csr_survival.S`) had gone
  dead in the 2-phase redesign (its readback `phase_c` sat after the exit
  marker, on the deleted QEMU2 leg), so nothing flagged the regression.

  "safe" envelope, so that envelope list was incomplete.

  - vsim resume: restored via the tolerant CSR write right after `mtvec`

  - vsim drain: re-read from the hart in `drain_with_passthrough`, so an

after write) and the PMP block for S/U handoffs (`resume_driver.hpp`).
`mscratch` is also re-read at drain and compared by `--verify` (L23).

### Transport ceiling - why "all CSRs" is not free

Three surfaces, three ceilings:

| Surface         | Mechanism                                     | Ceiling |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
| QEMU1 drain     | plugin reads by NAME from gdbstub XML         | only CSRs the QEMU fork advertises |
| vsim resume     | DMI Abstract Cmd + Program Buffer (by number) | RO / WARL / locked bits will not take arbitrary values |
| vsim drain      | DMI Abstract read (by number)                 | general for any readable CSR |

Two structural blockers to "all CSRs":

1. Wire format is a fixed C struct; `reserved[208]` fits about 26 more
   `uint64`. Reaching the full M + S + HPM + Andes set needs a v2 layout.
2. Semantics, not just bits. Restore order and side effects already bite
   (`mstatus.FS/VS` gating, `vsetvl` atomicity for `vtype/vl`). Writing
   `satp` flushes the TLB; Andes `mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` toggle caches,
   prefetchers, branch prediction and may be RO or locked when written
   via the debug module mid-run. Those are exactly the CSRs that shape
   the cycle figure.

Verdict: extending the wire format to a bounded set in this way is
feasible - the L20 fix is the worked example (one `uint64` carved from
`reserved[]`, drained by name, restored via the existing
abstract-or-PB write, read back at drain). S-mode trap CSRs and a
chosen Andes microarch subset can follow the same recipe.
"All RISC-V CSRs including Andes-specific" is not feasible without
redesigning the wire format and lifting the entire ROI envelope (L2-L6)."

### L15. Value-level handoff check: shipped for marker/pc, missing for icount/simpoint  (F-T3.1)

- When it bites: any bug that copies the wrong register, byte-swaps, or
  truncates a 64-bit value in the icount or simpoint paths.
- What happens: `run --verify` (marker/pc only, dev tier) re-runs the ELF
  on a pure-QEMU oracle and diffs the FULL drained state field by field
  (`driver/cmd_run.cpp:245-282`); `--cosim [--cosim-interval N]` goes
  further and localizes a divergence to the first bad N-retire window
  (it suppresses the cycle figure - the checkpoint drains pollute it; rerun
  without `--cosim` to measure). Both are manual, not CI-wired. The icount
  trigger and the SimPoint pipeline (`hsim.py`) still assert only exit code
  and PC range - a wrong register value there passes silently.
- Where: `driver/cmd_run.cpp:156` (marker/pc gate), `:245-282` (oracle);
  `hsim.py` (`_run_drain_pair`, `_run_simpoint_pipeline`) - unchecked.
- Status: PARTIALLY CLOSED (2026-06): marker/pc covered by
  `--verify`/`--cosim`; icount + simpoint coverage and CI wiring still OPEN.

### L22. Lock-step co-sim cannot handle asynchronous interrupts  (new 2026-06-15)

- When it bites: a `--model cycle --cosim` DV run whose testbench takes a
  timer / software / external interrupt (anything NOT caused by the current
  instruction). Synchronous exceptions (`ecall`, illegal, `mret`) ARE
  supported - this is only about async interrupts.
- What happens: the QEMU oracle and the RTL DUT run on independent clocks
  (QEMU is functional with no real cycles, the RTL is cycle-accurate), so
  each takes the same interrupt at a DIFFERENT retired-instruction index.
  Records are aligned by attempt index, so from the interrupt onward every
  record compares handler-vs-mainloop and the diff reports a flood of false
  divergences. Testbenches must be interrupt-free today.
- Where: `cosim_redesign.md` Usage 1 ("Out of scope / hard assumptions");
  the lock-step path in `driver/cosim_lockstep.cpp`, `driver/run_plan.cpp`.
- Status: OPEN. Designed fix is the opt-in `--cosim-async` mode (the RTL
  leads the interrupt schedule, QEMU replays it via an inject hook + a
  frozen timer) - features F8-F10 in `cosim_redesign.md`, not yet built.
  Distinct from L4 / the ROI envelope rule, which make the HYBRID
  measurement window interrupt-free; L22 is the lock-step DV path, which
  otherwise DOES support synchronous traps.

- The QEMU2 leg restored CSRs by gdbstub name and skipped quietly when the

- Status: REMOVED.

- The handback's fixed 10 s gdbstub timeout and TOCTOU port pick died with
  the leg.
- Status: REMOVED.

### L18. Wire format is little-endian / same-arch only

- When it bites: running any component on a big-endian host, or mixing
  hosts with different struct alignment.
- What happens: the state struct is exchanged byte-for-byte with no
  byte-swap path (`state_abi.h:7-9`). The Python mirror (golden only) uses
  a native-endian `ctypes.Structure` (`abi.py:28-31`), so a BE host would
  mis-parse the body while the `<II` magic check still passes - a silent
  mis-read.
- Where: `state_abi.h:7-9`, `abi.py:28-31`.
- Status: by design (x86-64 host + RV64 guest only).

### L19. Other un-guarded failure paths  (F-T3.3, F-T3.5, F-T3.6, F-T3.8)

- Determinism is not guaranteed across re-runs (reserved bytes, CSR drain

- Submodule version drift (QEMU plugin ABI, vsim DM, pinned SimPoint
  `17783e5`) has no CI gate.
- Failure injection is thin: partial drain, disk full, mmap truncated
  mid-run are not covered.
- Status: all OPEN, lower priority."

content.text:
Done. `mscratch` now round-trips across the handoff; the break is fixed via TDD (RED → GREEN), proven by the simulator's own oracle.

## What changed

**Root-cause fix (3 code changes):**
- `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` — restore `mscratch` into vsim (tolerant CSR write after `mtvec`; no FP/V gate — it's plain M-mode state). Closes the **resume gap**.
- `verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp` — `drain_with_passthrough` now re-reads `mscratch` from the hart instead of passing the QEMU1 value through. Closes the **drain gap**.
- `driver/state_diff.cpp` (+ `.hpp`) — `--verify` now compares `mscratch` (hybrid policy; still excluded in lock-step, where it's reset-vs-reset like `mstatus`/`mtval`). Closes the **verify blind spot**.

**Tests (TDD, all RED first then GREEN):**
- `resume_driver.test.cpp` — asserts `mscratch` is restored (and removed `0x340` from the stale "must NOT program" test).
- `state_drain.test.cpp` — asserts the drain re-reads `mscratch`.
- `state_diff_test.cpp` — asserts `mscratch` is compared in hybrid, excluded in lock-step (+ updated counts).
- Full host suite: 20/20 hybrid doctests + state_diff pass; the only non-build (`kanata_roi`) is a pre-existing host-only spdlog/fmt link issue.

**Regression guard:** revived the dead `tests/fixtures/rt_csr_survival.S` for the 2-phase design — it self-checks the `mscratch` round-trip *inside* the ROI (spins → timeout on regression, so it works in the plain e2e suite without `--verify`). Folded the PoC `break_mscratch.S` into it.

**Docs:** CLAUDE.md "CSR restore split"; limitations notebook (cell-3, cell-6 inventories corrected, new **L23** entry, quick-ref row, scorecard blocker 4).

## Proof
- The original break program now **PASSES** `--verify`: `[state-diff] PASS: 111 fields match` (was `x10 ref=0xcafe... got=0x0`).
- `rt_csr_survival` passes marker + pc + `VERIFY=1`.
- e2e subset (GPR/FP/V/shared-mem/csr, both modes): **10/10 pass** — no regression.

## Scope
Only `mscratch` — it's a side-effect-free software CSR legal in a trap-free ROI. The other drained-but-unrestored M-CSRs (`mepc/mcause/mtval/medeleg/mideleg/mip/mie`, `satp`) are trap/interrupt/paging machinery, deliberately left to the L3/L4 envelope work; `mtvec` is restored but still not re-drained. I didn't commit anything (working tree was already dirty at session start).

content.text:
Answer: on the default engine, all the M-mode trap CSRs are supported on both sides, but `satp`/`medeleg`/`mideleg` are NOT implemented by the RTL - so my earlier "deferred" label was wrong for those three.

## What "supported" means here
- Producer = QEMU gdbstub. A CSR is drained only if its predicate passes (`gdbstub.c:270`); a missing one resolves to NULL and `read_reg64` silently drains 0.
- Consumer = vsim RTL via DMI abstract command. A CSR the core doesn't implement makes the abstract write raise `cmderr` (tolerated as a no-op) and the readback return 0.

Default pair: QEMU `-cpu andes-ax45mpv` (`engine_registry.cpp:46`) <-> RTL `ax45mpv_premium`, which is **M-mode only** (`config.inc:126`, `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS 1`).

## Per-CSR result (default engine)

| CSR | QEMU drains? | RTL implements? (restore/re-read) | Restored today |
|-----|----|----|----|
| mstatus | yes (`any`) | yes | yes (FP/V only) |
| mtvec | yes (`any`) | yes | yes |
| mscratch | yes (`any`) | yes | yes (L23) |
| mepc / mcause / mtval | yes (`any`) | yes | **no - genuinely deferred** |
| mip / mie | yes (`any`) | yes | **no - genuinely deferred** |
| mcycle / minstret | yes | yes | yes |
| **satp** | yes* | **NO (S-mode CSR, M-only core)** | no |
| **medeleg / mideleg** | yes (`any`) | **NO (need S-mode)** | no |

\* QEMU `-cpu andes-ax45mpv` advertises `RVS|RVU` (`cpu.c` ax45 init, misa = `...RVS|RVU|RVV...`), so its gdbstub *does* expose `satp` (predicate `satp`->`smode`->`riscv_has_ext(RVS)` passes). The RTL it's paired with does not implement it.

## The finding
There's an asymmetry: **QEMU is S/U/M-capable, but the default RTL is M-only.** So QEMU drains real `satp`/`medeleg`/`mideleg` values that the default engine physically cannot accept.

This corrects my earlier summary. The drained-but-unrestored set splits into two:
- `mepc / mcause / mtval / mip / mie` - supported on both sides, just not written back. "Deferred to L3/L4" is accurate.
- `satp / medeleg / mideleg` - **not implemented on the default engine at all**; nothing to restore there. They only become real on the S/U-capable `ax66_makatau` engine. Calling them "deferred" on the default engine was inaccurate.

`mtvec` is restored but still not re-drained at exit (asymmetric, like the pre-L23 `mscratch` state).

content.text:
Design decision (mirrors L23 mscratch, with one nuance):

- **Restore + re-read at drain + verify**: `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mie` - symmetric round-trip like mscratch.
- **mip**: restore + re-read but **excluded from --verify**. Its pending bits (MTIP/MEIP/MSIP) are hardware/platform-driven; MTIP tracks elapsed time, which advances differently in QEMU (functional) vs vsim (cycle-accurate), so it legitimately diverges even in a trap-free ROI. On the M-only default engine the restore is a no-op (M pending bits are read-only via CSR), but it does real work on S-capable engines.
- `mepc`/`mcause` become compared in **both** hybrid and lock-step; `mtval`/`mie`/`mscratch` stay hybrid-only (lock-step keeps `mtval` excluded as impl-defined on real traps).

cd /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim

## The core rule: the vsim measurement window (ROI) is very narrow

This is the single most important limitation. Everything in Tier 1 is a
consequence of it.

When execution hands off to vsim, the resume step writes back only a small
part of the CPU state. Read `resume_driver.hpp`: it restores GPRs,
FPRs, the V registers, PC, six CSRs - `mstatus`, `mtvec`,

===== CELL 3 =====
## The core rule: the vsim measurement window (ROI) is very narrow

This is the single most important limitation. Everything in Tier 1 is a
consequence of it.

When execution hands off to vsim, the resume step writes back only a small
part of the CPU state. Read `resume_driver.hpp`: it restores GPRs,
FPRs, the V registers, PC, six CSRs - `mstatus`, `mtvec`,
`mcycle`, `minstret`, `fcsr` (since L20, 2026-06-12), and `mscratch`
(since L23, 2026-06-15) - plus, since
L6 (2026-06-13), the privilege level via `dcsr.prv` (write-verified) and,
for S/U-privilege handoffs only, the PMP block.
It does NOT write `satp`, `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`,
`medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie` - and for M-mode
handoffs PMP stays unrestored too (L2).

The cell below prints the complete CSR list the resume driver knows. Note
what is still missing: no `satp`, no `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`.

===== CELL 6 =====
## State coverage: what the wire format carries

Inventory view of the ROI rule above. Everything below is checked against
`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (struct), the QEMU plugin drain
(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`), the vsim resume (`resume_driver.hpp`),
and the vsim drain (`state_drain.hpp`).

### Carried in `hybrid_state_v1`

- 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs
- `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags; added 2026-06-12, closing L20)
- 13 M-mode CSRs: `mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch,
  medeleg, mideleg, mip, mie, mcycle, minstret, satp`
- PMP: 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
- V extension: `vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, vreg[32], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr`
- F13 warmup metadata: `mcycle_at_measure_start`, `minstret_at_measure_start`
- `reserved[208]` = room for ~26 more `uint64` (wire format is version 2
  since L11 widened `vreg[]` to 128 bytes per register)

### NOT in the wire format at all

- All S-mode CSRs: `stvec, sepc, scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip,
  scounteren, senvcfg, stimecmp`
- HPM block: `mhpmcounter3..31`, `mhpmevent3..31`, `mcounteren,
  menvcfg, mcountinhibit, mconfigptr, misa, time`
- Every Andes-custom CSR (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec`, ...). See L21.

### Carried but NOT restored into vsim

The QEMU1 plugin drains them into the struct, but `ResumeDriver`
writes none of them into the vsim hart. They are dead during the ROI:

- `satp` (L3), `mepc / mcause / mtval` (L4), and `medeleg, mideleg,
  mip, mie` (L2/L4 -- trap/interrupt machinery). (`mscratch` left this
  set in L23: it is a side-effect-free software CSR and round-trips
  now.) PMP is restored only for S/U-privilege handoffs (L6,
  2026-06-13) -- without it an S/U ROI cannot fetch on a
  PMP-implementing core; M-mode handoffs keep PMP pass-through-only.

CSRs actually restored into vsim: `mstatus, mtvec, mscratch (L23),
mcycle, minstret, fcsr`, plus `dcsr.prv` (the privilege level, verified
after write) and the PMP block for S/U handoffs (`resume_driver.hpp`).
`mscratch` is also re-read at drain and compared by `--verify` (L23).

### Transport ceiling - why "all CSRs" is not free

Three surfaces, three ceilings:

| Surface         | Mechanism                                     | Ceiling |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
| QEMU1 drain     | plugin reads by NAME from gdbstub XML         | only CSRs the QEMU fork advertises |
| vsim resume     | DMI Abstract Cmd + Program Buffer (by number) | RO / WARL / locked bits will not take arbitrary values |
| vsim drain      | DMI Abstract read (by number)                 | general for any readable CSR |

Two structural blockers to "all CSRs":

1. Wire format is a fixed C struct; `reserved[208]` fits about 26 more
   `uint64`. Reaching the full M + S + HPM + Andes set needs a v2 layout.
2. Semantics, not just bits. Restore order and side effects already bite
   (`mstatus.FS/VS` gating, `vsetvl` atomicity for `vtype/vl`). Writing
   `satp` flushes the TLB; Andes `mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` toggle caches,
   prefetchers, branch prediction and may be RO or locked when written
   via the debug module mid-run. Those are exactly the CSRs that shape
   the cycle figure.

Verdict: extending the wire format to a bounded set in this way is
feasible - the L20 fix is the worked example (one `uint64` carved from
`reserved[]`, drained by name, restored via the existing
abstract-or-PB write, read back at drain). S-mode trap CSRs and a
chosen Andes microarch subset can follow the same recipe.
"All RISC-V CSRs including Andes-specific" is not feasible without
redesigning the wire format and lifting the entire ROI envelope (L2-L6).

===== CELL 16 =====
## Quick reference

| ID  | Limitation                              | Severity | Status |
|-----|-----------------------------------------|----------|--------|
| L1  | Semihosting in ROI fatal; vplat is the supported I/O path | blocker | resolved in-tree |
| L2  | PMP not restored to vsim (M-mode handoffs; S/U mirror it since L6) | high | partial |
| L3  | Paging (satp) off in ROI                | high     | open   |
| L4  | Trap state lost across ROI              | high     | open   |
| L5  | LR/SC cannot cross handoff              | high     | open   |
| L6  | Privilege forced to M-mode              | high     | resolved |
| L7  | No workload-fits-RAM check; 2 GiB hard max | medium | open   |
| L8  | Single hart only                        | medium   | open   |
| L9  | MMIO in ROI: vplat device set only      | medium   | partial |
| L10 | Engines pluggable; machine + scratch GPA fixed | medium | partial |
| L11 | VLEN ceiling 1024; over-limit aborts loudly | medium | resolved |
| L12 | CSR 0x7C0 trigger collision             | low      | resolved |
| L13 | Marker must be 32-bit                   | low      | resolved |
| L14 | SimPoint estimate is approximate        | medium   | by design |
| L15 | Value-level check: marker/pc only       | medium   | partial |
| L16 | CSR restore silently skipped if missing | medium   | removed |
| L17 | Fixed gdbstub timeout + racy port       | low      | removed |
| L18 | Little-endian / same-arch only          | low      | by design |
| L19 | Determinism / drift / fault-injection   | low      | open   |
| L20 | fcsr/frm/fflags not transported         | high     | resolved |
| L21 | Andes vendor CSRs not transported       | high     | open   |
| L22 | Async interrupts unsupported in lock-step cosim | medium | open |
| L23 | mscratch software CSR not restored / re-read    | high   | resolved |

===== CELL 17 =====
## Commercial product quality rating  (assessed 2026-05-28)

> Re-check 2026-06-12: five areas moved since this assessment. The vplat
> runtime gives a supported I/O path inside the ROI (L1/L9; every in-tree
> C fixture now links it, so L1 is resolved in-tree); `--verify` and
> `--cosim` add a value-level oracle check for marker/pc runs (L15); engines
> are drop-in with VLEN synced from the descriptor, and L11 is now
> resolved (2026-06-12): the wire format carries VLEN 128..1024 and an
> over-ceiling vlenb aborts loudly instead of truncating (L10 partial); the marker
> HINT trigger retired the CSR-collision caveats (L12/L13); and `fcsr`
> now round-trips with an FP-rounding fixture in the e2e suite (L20
> resolved - five CSRs restore into vsim now, and the silent FP-rounding
> gap in blocker 1 below is closed). L6 is resolved (2026-06-13): the privilege
> level round-trips (plugin gdbstub `priv` -> `dcsr.prv` write+verify ->
> exit-drain readback), S/U handoffs mirror the producer's PMP block
> (L2 partial), an M-only engine aborts loudly, and `rt_priv_smode` /
> `rt_priv_umode` run in the e2e suite on the ax66_makatau engine. The
> remaining state coverage and ROI envelope items (L2-L5, L21) are
> unchanged, so the overall scores below still stand.
>
> Re-check 2026-06-15: `mscratch` now round-trips too (L23) -- a sixth CSR
> restored into vsim, re-read at drain, and compared by `--verify`; blocker 4
> below is updated. Still a narrow envelope (L2-L5, L21 unchanged).

Honest scorecard for "is this a shippable commercial product today?".
Rated against industry baselines (Synopsys VCS, Cadence Xcelium,
gem5 + functional warmup) for a CPU vendor's hybrid sim offering.

**Overall: 4/10 as a shippable commercial product. ~7/10 as an internal
/ research tool inside its narrow design envelope.**

### Axis breakdown

| Axis                                  | Score | Note |
|---------------------------------------|-------|------|
| Architecture clarity                  | 8/10  | Two-phase handoff is clean; shared ABI is a single header. |
| Engineering discipline                | 7/10  | TDD gate, doctest, parallel CI, a candid limitations doc. |
| State coverage (correctness surface)  | 3/10  | 22 documented limitations; only 6 CSRs round-trip into vsim. |
| Generality of workload                | 2/10  | ROI must be single-privilege (M/S/U since L6), trap-free, paging-off (L1-L5). |
| ISA completeness                      | 3/10  | ~~No S/U mode~~ (L6 2026-06-13), ~~no fcsr~~ (L20); still no HPM, zero Andes vendor CSRs (vendor IS Andes). |
| Wire-format extensibility             | 4/10  | v1 only; growth happens by carving `reserved[216]` ad-hoc. No v2 path. |
| Robustness / errors                   | 5/10  | `cmderr` is cleared and swallowed; only a private diagnostic side channel. |
| Docs / onboarding                     | 7/10  | `CLAUDE.md`, `USER_GUIDE.md`, and this notebook are unusually honest. |
| Test fixtures                         | 6/10  | Solid asm + C-runtime e2e; FP-rounding (rt_c_fcsr) and S/U-privilege (rt_priv_*) covered now; still no trap fixtures. |
| Portability                           | 4/10  | x86-64 host + little-endian assumed (L18); pinned Andes toolchain; podman-only vsim build. |

### What blocks commercial shipping

1. **Silent correctness gaps.** ~~`fcsr/frm/fflags` never round-trip
   (L20)~~ - resolved 2026-06-12; `fcsr` now transports and `--verify`
   compares it. Still standing: `cmderr` is W1C-cleared so a partial CSR
   restore is observable only through a private counter
   (`resume_driver.hpp:196-205`).
2. **ROI envelope is too narrow.** ~~M-mode only~~ (S/U privilege
   transports since L6, 2026-06-13, on an S/U-capable engine), but "no
   traps, no paging, no semihosting inside the window" (L1-L5) still
   rules out every real OS-bearing benchmark - SPEC under Linux, any
   driver code, anything with page faults. The vplat runtime covers
   bare-metal I/O only.
3. **No Andes vendor CSRs.** For an Andes product, shipping zero
   `mmsc_cfg / mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` transport (L21) is a
   credibility hit and an accuracy hazard - cache and prefetcher
   controls shape the cycle count.
4. **Only 6 CSRs restored into vsim** (mstatus, mtvec, mscratch, mcycle,
   minstret, fcsr), plus `dcsr.prv` and - for S/U handoffs - the PMP
   block (L6, 2026-06-13). `satp`, `mepc/mcause/mtval`,
   `mip/mie` (and PMP on M-mode handoffs) are drained but never written
   back into vsim (`resume_driver.hpp`). They exist in the wire format
   but not in the simulator. Any future need for traps or dynamic
   PMP needs `resume_driver` extended.
5. **Wire format is v1-locked with ad-hoc growth.** Each new field
   steals from `reserved[]` (warmup metadata ate 16 bytes, fcsr another
   8; `state_abi.h`). No deprecation path, no feature bits beyond
   the three `HYBRID_FLAG_*` bits.
6. **Build/test infrastructure is single-host.** Podman-required vsim
   build, hardcoded `JOBS=8` ceiling on 128-core hosts,
   `/dev/shm`-backed fixtures - all fine for a lab, painful for a
   commercial CI matrix.

### What it does well (the 7/10 internal-tool score)

- Two-phase handoff is a clear, documented contract.
- `state_abi.h` plus `static_assert`s pin layout - good ABI hygiene.
- The team writes down what does NOT work (this notebook, 22 entries plus
  the state-coverage section) instead of hiding it. Commercially that
  is the release-blocker checklist; internally it is exemplary.
- SimPoint integration for whole-program cycle estimation (L14) is a
  real differentiator over a pure functional sim.

### Bottom line

Ship-grade architecture, research-grade coverage. For commercial
release you need:

- v2 wire format with feature bits and a deprecation path
- traps + paging supported inside ROI (close L3, L4);
  ~~privilege transport (L6)~~ done 2026-06-13
- Andes vendor CSR transport (close L21)
- ~~`fcsr` fix (close L20)~~ done 2026-06-12
- A proper error policy instead of `cmderr` swallowing
- The existing `--verify`/`--cosim` oracle (L15) extended to
  icount/simpoint and wired into CI

Rough effort: 6-9 months of focused hardening, not weeks.

| Surface         | Mechanism                                     | Ceiling |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
| QEMU1 drain     | plugin reads by NAME from gdbstub XML         | only CSRs the QEMU fork advertises |
| vsim resume     | DMI Abstract Cmd + Program Buffer (by number) | RO / WARL / locked bits will not take arbitrary values |
| vsim drain      | DMI Abstract read (by number)                 | general for any readable CSR |

Two structural blockers to "all CSRs":

1. Wire format is a fixed C struct; `reserved[208]` fits about 26 more
   `uint64`. Reaching the full M + S + HPM + Andes set needs a v2 layout.
2. Semantics, not just bits. Restore order and side effects already bite
   (`mstatus.FS/VS` gating, `vsetvl` atomicity for `vtype/vl`). Writing
   `satp` flushes the TLB; Andes `mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` toggle caches,
   prefetchers, branch prediction and may be RO or locked when written
   via the debug module mid-run. Those are exactly the CSRs that shape
   the cycle figure.

Verdict: extending the wire format to a bounded set in this way is
feasible - the L20 fix is the worked example (one `uint64` carved from
`reserved[]`, drained by name, restored via the existing
abstract-or-PB write, read back at drain). S-mode trap CSRs and a
chosen Andes microarch subset can follow the same recipe.
"All RISC-V CSRs including Andes-specific" is not feasible without
redesigning the wire format and lifting the entire ROI envelope (L2-L6).

===== CELL 16 =====
## Quick reference

| ID  | Limitation                              | Severity | Status |
|-----|-----------------------------------------|----------|--------|
| L1  | Semihosting in ROI fatal; vplat is the supported I/O path | blocker | resolved in-tree |
| L2  | PMP not restored to vsim (M-mode handoffs; S/U mirror it since L6) | high | partial |
| L3  | Paging (satp) off in ROI                | high     | open   |
| L4  | Trap state lost across ROI              | high     | open   |
| L5  | LR/SC cannot cross handoff              | high     | open   |
| L6  | Privilege forced to M-mode              | high     | resolved |
| L7  | No workload-fits-RAM check; 2 GiB hard max | medium | open   |
| L8  | Single hart only                        | medium   | open   |
| L9  | MMIO in ROI: vplat device set only      | medium   | partial |
| L10 | Engines pluggable; machine + scratch GPA fixed | medium | partial |
| L11 | VLEN ceiling 1024; over-limit aborts loudly | medium | resolved |
| L12 | CSR 0x7C0 trigger collision             | low      | resolved |
| L13 | Marker must be 32-bit                   | low      | resolved |
| L14 | SimPoint estimate is approximate        | medium   | by design |
| L15 | Value-level check: marker/pc only       | medium   | partial |
| L16 | CSR restore silently skipped if missing | medium   | removed |
| L17 | Fixed gdbstub timeout + racy port       | low      | removed |
| L18 | Little-endian / same-arch only          | low      | by design |
| L19 | Determinism / drift / fault-injection   | low      | open   |
| L20 | fcsr/frm/fflags not transported         | high     | resolved |
| L21 | Andes vendor CSRs not transported       | high     | open   |
